headings: Pricing of Our Products and Services
paragraphs: We are a leading broadband connectivity company with services available to 58 million homes and small to large businesses across 41 states through our Spectrum® brand. Founded in 1993, we have evolved from providing cable TV to streaming, and from high-speed Internet to a converged broadband, WiFi and mobile experience. Over the Spectrum Fiber Broadband Network and supported by our 100% U.S.-based employees, we offer Seamless Connectivity and Entertainment with Spectrum Internet®, Mobile, TV and Voice products.

Our strategy is focused on utilizing our fiber-powered network to deliver high-quality, competitively priced products, with outstanding service, allowing us to increase both the number of customers we serve over our network and the number of products we sell to each customer. This combination also reduces the number of service transactions we perform per relationship, yielding higher customer satisfaction and lower customer churn, which results in lower costs to acquire and serve customers and drives greater profitability.

We offer Spectrum Internet products with speeds up to 1 gigabits per second ("Gbps") across our entire footprint and multi-gigabit speeds in a portion of our footprint. We continue to upgrade our connectivity network, and we will offer symmetrical and multi-gigabit Internet speeds across our entire footprint in the next several years. Advanced WiFi, a managed WiFi service that provides customers an optimized home network while providing greater control of connected devices with enhanced security and privacy, is available to all of our Internet customers. Spectrum Mobile® is available to all new and existing Spectrum Internet customers and offers plans that include 5G access, do not require contracts and include taxes and fees in the price. We continue to innovate our video product and have transformed all of our affiliation agreements with major programmers. These new agreements give us greater overall packaging flexibility and the ability to include the ad-supported versions of key programmer streaming applications, at no extra cost, within our video packages, along with the ability to upgrade to ad-free versions and to sell those applications to customers a la carte for a seamless entertainment experience. Together with our Xumo Stream Boxes ("Xumo"), our goal is to deliver utility and value for our customers, irrespective of how they want to view content, and better and more stable economics for our programming partners and us.

Our fully deployed fiber-powered network offers ubiquitous and seamless connectivity products. It removes barriers and creates opportunities for customers, in every aspect of their lives. Our brand platform, Life Unlimited™, emphasizes the power of our advanced network and cutting-edge connectivity products and services, and our simplified pricing strategy better utilizes our seamless connectivity and entertainment products to offer lower promotional and persistent bundled pricing to drive growth. Additionally, our customer commitments focus on reliable connectivity, transparency, exceptional service and always improving. Through reliable connectivity, we are committed to keeping our customers connected 100% of the time and promptly resolving issues. Transparency at every step means we provide clear and simple pricing and timely service updates, and we take responsibility when things go wrong. Through exceptional service, we provide exceptional customer experiences. And finally, always improving means we act on our customers' feedback to improve our products and customer service.

Our network and product evolution plan continues to progress, with a clear path to delivering symmetrical and multi-gig speeds to customers across our footprint, meeting the needs of today and anticipating the growing demand for faster speeds for years to come. We continue to expand the capacity of our fiber-powered network using a number of technologies, including
•spectrum expansion, initially to 1.2 GHz and then to 1.8 GHz; •changing the bandwidth allocation to a "high split" to increase upstream speeds;
•Distributed Access Architecture ("DAA"); and

Through this process, which we expect to be largely complete by the end of 2027, we will transform our network to offer much faster Internet speeds. Those faster Internet speeds will be offered in conjunction with our Spectrum Mobile product and
Advanced WiFi, providing customers seamless and convenient, ultra-fast converged connectivity in attractively priced packages.

Since inception in the beginning of 2022, we have spent $7.7 billion on our subsidized rural construction initiative and activated approximately 1.3 million passings. Rural footprint builds present strategic network expansion opportunities to deliver service to unserved and underserved passings. Our rural investments allow us to offer a suite of broadband connectivity services, including fixed Internet, WiFi and mobile to unserved areas in states where we currently operate. To accomplish all of this, we have invested in new construction teams and new equipment. These investments will allow us to generate long-term infrastructure-style returns by taking further advantage of our scale efficiencies, network quality and construction capabilities, while offering our high-quality products and services to more homes and businesses.

Our principal executive offices are located at 400 Washington Blvd., Stamford, Connecticut 06902. Our telephone number is (203) 905-7801, and we have a website accessible at ir.charter.com. The information posted on our website is not incorporated into this annual report.

headings: We operate in a very competitive business environment, which affects our ability to attract and retain customers and can adversely affect our business, operations and financial results.

Various events could disrupt or result in unauthorized access to our networks, information systems or properties and could impair our operating activities and negatively impact our reputation and financial results.
Any failure to respond to technological developments and meet customer demand for new products and services could adversely affect our ability to compete effectively.
Our business may be adversely affected if we cannot continue to license or enforce the intellectual property rights on which our business depends.
We may not have the ability to pass on to our customers all of the increases in programming costs, which could adversely affect our cash flow and operating margins.
Issues related to the development and use of AI could give rise to legal or regulatory action, damage our reputation or otherwise materially harm our business.
Our exposure to the economic conditions of our current and potential customers, vendors and third parties could adversely affect our cash flow, results of operations and financial condition.
If we are unable to retain key employees, our ability to manage our business could be adversely affected.

The agreements and instruments governing our debt contain restrictions and limitations that could significantly affect our ability to operate our business, as well as significantly affect our liquidity.

paragraphs: The industry in which we operate is highly competitive and has become more so in recent years. In some instances, we compete against companies with fewer regulatory burdens, better access to financing and greater and more favorable brand name recognition. Increasing consolidation in the telecommunications and content industries have provided additional benefits to certain of our competitors, either through access to financing, resources, or efficiencies of scale including the ability to launch new products and services.

Our Internet service faces competition from other companies' FTTH, cell phone home Internet service, Internet delivered via satellite and DSL services. Various operators offer wireless Internet services delivered over networks which they continue to enhance to deliver faster speeds and also continue to expand 5G mobile services as they seek to offer converged connectivity services similar to ours. Our mobile and voice services compete with wireless and wireline phone providers, as well as other forms of communication, such as text, instant messaging, social networking services, video conferencing and email. Competition from these companies, including intensive marketing efforts with aggressive pricing, may have an adverse impact on our ability to attract and retain customers.

Our video service faces competition from a number of sources, including DBS services, and companies that deliver linear network programming, movies and television shows on demand and other video content over broadband Internet connections to televisions, computers, tablets and mobile devices often with password sharing among multiple users and security that makes content susceptible to piracy. Newer products and services, particularly alternative methods for the distribution, sale and viewing of content may continue to be developed, further increasing the competition that we face.

The increasing number of choices available to audiences, including low-cost or free choices, could negatively impact not only consumer demand for our products and services, but also advertisers' willingness to purchase advertising from us. We compete for the sale of advertising revenue with television networks and stations, as well as other advertising platforms, such as online media, radio and print. Competition related to our service offerings to businesses continues to increase as well, as more companies deploy more fiber to more buildings, which may negatively impact our growth and put pressure on margins.

A failure to effectively anticipate or adapt to new technologies (including those that use artificial intelligence ("AI")) and changes in customer expectations and behavior could significantly adversely affect our competitive position with respect to the leisure time and discretionary spending of our customers and, as a result, affect our business and results of operations. Competition may also reduce our expected growth of future cash flows which may contribute to future impairments of our franchises and goodwill and our ability to meet cash flow requirements, including debt service requirements. For additional information regarding the competition we face, see "Item 1. Business - Competition" and "Item 1. Business - Regulation and Legislation."

Network and information systems technologies are critical to our operating activities, both for our internal uses, such as network management, and supplying services to our customers, including customer service operations and programming delivery. Network or information system shutdowns or other service disruptions caused by events such as computer hacking, phishing, dissemination of computer viruses, worms and other destructive or disruptive software, malicious cyber activities by nation-state threat actors, "cyber attacks" such as ransomware, process breakdowns, denial of service attacks and other malicious activity pose increasing risks. Both unsuccessful and successful "cyber attacks" on companies have continued to increase in frequency, scope and potential harm in recent years, and the increasing use of AI may intensify these cybersecurity risks. While we develop and maintain systems seeking to prevent systems-related events and security breaches from occurring, the development and maintenance of these systems is costly and requires ongoing monitoring and updating as techniques used in such attacks become more sophisticated and change frequently. We, and the third parties on which we rely, may be unable to anticipate these techniques or implement adequate preventive measures. While from time to time attempts have been made to access our network, these events have not as yet resulted in any material release of information, degradation or disruption to our network and information systems.

Risk Factors" and "Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements," which describe important factors that could cause actual results to differ from expectations and non-historical information contained herein. In addition, the following discussion should be read in conjunction with the audited consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes thereto of Charter included in "Part II. Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data."

We are a leading broadband connectivity company with services available to 58 million homes and small to large businesses across 41 states through our Spectrum brand. Founded in 1993, we have evolved from providing cable TV to streaming, and from high-speed Internet to a converged broadband, WiFi and mobile experience. Over the Spectrum Fiber Broadband Network and supported by our 100% U.S.-based employees, we offer Seamless Connectivity and Entertainment with Spectrum Internet, Mobile, TV and Voice products. See "Part I. Item 1. Business — Products and Services" for further description of these services, including customer statistics for different services.

During the year ended December 31, 2025, we added 1.9 million mobile lines while Internet and video losses improved as compared to the prior year period. Sales were challenged by the competitive environment but were offset by lower customer churn. We remain focused on improving customer results through our brand platform, Life Unlimited which emphasizes the power of our advanced fiber-powered network and cutting-edge connectivity products and services, and our simplified pricing and packaging strategy that better utilizes our seamless connectivity and entertainment products to offer lower promotional and persistent bundled pricing to drive growth. Our Internet and mobile product bundles provide a differentiated connectivity experience by bringing together Spectrum Internet, Advanced WiFi and Unlimited Spectrum Mobile to offer consumers fast, reliable and secure online connections on their favorite devices at home and on the go in high-value packages. We have completed deals with major programmers to deliver better flexibility and greater value to our customers by including seamless entertainment applications with certain of our Spectrum TV packages at no additional cost. In July 2025, we began launching the sale of these seamless entertainment applications to customers on an à la carte basis, and we recently launched the Spectrum App Store, a digital storefront that helps customers activate, upgrade, buy and manage their streaming applications in one place. We also continue to evolve other elements of our video product and are deploying Xumo stream boxes to new video customers.

Our customer commitments focus on reliable connectivity, transparency, exceptional service and always improving. By continually improving our product set and offering consumers the opportunity to save money by switching to our services, we believe we can continue to penetrate our expanding footprint and sell additional products to our existing customers. We see operational benefits from the targeted investments we made in employee wages and benefits to build employee skill sets and tenure, as well as the continued investments in digitization of our customer service platforms, all with the goal of improving the customer experience, reducing transactions and driving customer growth and retention.

We spent $2.2 billion on our subsidized rural construction initiative during the year ended December 31, 2025 and activated approximately 483,000 subsidized rural passings. We currently offer Spectrum Internet products with speeds up to 1 Gbps across our entire footprint and multi-gigabit data speeds in a portion of our footprint. Our network evolution initiative remains on track to deliver symmetrical and multi-gigabit speeds across our entire footprint with convergence everywhere we operate.

Total revenues decreased slightly primarily due to lower customers, higher seamless entertainment allocation and lower advertising sales, partly offset by mobile line growth and higher average revenue per customer. Adjusted EBITDA grew slightly with mobile revenues growing at a faster rate than mobile direct costs. Income from operations was further negatively impacted by an increase in loss on disposal of assets and merger and acquisition costs.

Approximately 89% of our revenues for each of the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 are attributable to monthly subscription fees charged to customers for our Internet, mobile, video, voice and commercial services as well as regional sports and news channels. Generally, these customer subscriptions may be discontinued by the customer at any time subject to a fee for certain commercial customers. The remaining 11% of our revenue is derived primarily from advertising revenues, franchise and other regulatory fee revenues (which are collected by us but then paid to local authorities), sales of mobile and video devices, processing fees or reconnection fees charged to customers to commence or reinstate service, installation, VOD and pay-per-view programming, and commissions related to the sale of merchandise by home shopping services.

Costs associated with network construction or upgrades, placement of the customer drop to the dwelling and the placement of outlets within a dwelling along with the costs associated with the deployment of new customer premise equipment necessary to provide Internet, video or voice services, are capitalized. Costs capitalized include materials, direct labor and certain indirect costs. These indirect costs consist of compensation and overhead costs associated with support functions. While our capitalization is based on specific activities, once capitalized, we track these costs on a composite basis by fixed asset category at the cable system level, and not on a specific asset basis. For assets that are sold or retired, we remove the estimated applicable cost and accumulated depreciation. The costs of disconnecting service and removing customer premise equipment from a dwelling and the costs to reconnect a customer drop or to redeploy previously installed customer premise equipment are charged to operating expense as incurred. Costs for repairs and maintenance are charged to operating expense as incurred, while plant and equipment replacement, including replacement of certain components, betterments, and replacement of cable drops and outlets, are capitalized.

We make judgments regarding the installation and construction activities to be capitalized. paragraphs: 本公司為一間領導的寬頻連線公司，透過我們的 Spectrum® 品牌，提供服務至美國 41 個州的 58 百萬戶家庭及中小企業。自 1993 年成立以來，我們已從提供有線電視服務，進化為串流服務，並從高速網路服務，進化為整合型寬頻、WiFi 及行動服務的體驗。透過 Spectrum Fiber Broadband 網路，並由我們 100% 美國本土員工支持，我們提供 Seamless Connectivity 和娛樂服務，包括 Spectrum Internet®、行動、電視及語音產品。
我們的策略聚焦於利用我們的光纖網路，提供高品質且具競爭價格的產品，並搭配優越的服務，使我們能增加透過網路服務的客戶數量，以及每個客戶購買的產品數量。這種組合也減少我們每筆客戶關係執行的服務交易次數，提高客戶滿意度並降低客戶流失率，這會降低獲取與服務客戶的成本，並提高利潤。

我們提供 Spectrum Internet 產品，速度可達每秒 1 個 gigabits ("Gbps")，遍及我們所有服務範圍，並在部分服務範圍內提供多 gigabits 速度。我們持續升級我們的連線網路，並預計在未來幾年內，於我們所有服務範圍內提供對稱式與多 gigabits 的網際網路速度。進階 WiFi 是一種管理式 WiFi 服務，可為客戶提供最佳化家庭網路，並提供對連線裝置更大的控制權，並提升安全性與隱私權。此服務可供所有網際網路客戶使用。Spectrum Mobile® 可供所有新舊 Spectrum Internet 客戶使用，並提供包含 5G 連線的方案，不需簽約，且價格已包含稅費。我們持續創新我們的視訊產品，並已與主要內容供應商重新簽訂所有合作協議。這些新協議使我們擁有更靈活的內容包裝選擇，並可在我們的視訊方案中，免費包含主要內容供應商串流應用的廣告支援版本，同時也允許升級為無廣告版本，並可將這些應用軟體以 a la carte 方式銷售給客戶，以提供無縫的娛樂體驗。與我們的 Xumo Stream Boxes ("Xumo") 結合，我們的目標是為客戶提供無論如何觀看內容的實用與價值，並為我們的內容供應商與我們帶來更好的穩定經濟效益。

我們已完全部署的光纖網路，提供普遍且無縫的連線產品。這會消除客戶在生活各方面的障礙，並創造機會。我們的品牌平台 Life Unlimited™ 強調我們先進網路與尖端連線產品與服務的強大功能，並透過簡化定價策略，更有效地利用我們的無縫連線與娛樂產品，提供較低的促銷與持續的捆綁定價，以推動成長。此外，我們的客戶承諾聚焦於可靠連線、透明度、卓越服務與持續改善。透過可靠連線，我們承諾讓客戶 100% 時刻保持連線，並迅速解決問題。透明度在每一步驟中意味著我們提供清晰且簡易的定價與及時的服務更新，並在事情出錯時承擔責任。透過卓越服務，我們提供卓越的客戶體驗。最後，持續改善意味著我們根據客戶的意見改進產品與客戶服務。
我們的網路與產品演進計畫持續進行中，並有明確的路徑可提供對稱式與多 gigabits 速度給我們服務範圍內的客戶，以符合當前需求並預見未來對更快速度的成長需求。我們持續透過多種技術擴充我們的光纖網路容量，包括
•光譜擴展，最初至 1.2 GHz，然後至 1.8 GHz；•改變頻寬分配至 "high split" 以提高上行速度；
•分散式存取架構 ("DAA")；以及
透過這個過程，我們預期在 2027 年底前 largely 完成，我們將轉型網路以提供更快的網際網路速度。這些更快的網際網路速度將與我們的 Spectrum Mobile 產品一同提供
Advanced WiFi，提供客戶無縫且便利、超高速的整合式連線服務，並以具吸引力的價格包裝。

自2022年初開始運作以來，我們已投入77億美元於我們的補貼式鄉村建設計畫，並啟動約130萬個服務點。鄉村服務點的建設，提供了戰略性的網路擴張機會，以提供服務給未被服務及服務不足的服務點。我們的鄉村投資使我們能夠提供一系列的寬頻連線服務，包括固定網路、WiFi及行動服務，至我們目前運作的州內未被服務的地區。為達成所有這些目標，我們已投資於新的建設團隊及新設備。這些投資將使我們能產生長期基礎建設類型的回報，透過進一步利用我們的規模效益、網路品質及建設能力，同時為更多家庭及企業提供我們的高品質產品與服務。

本公司主要營業據點位於 Connecticut 紐約州史達蒙 (Stamford, Connecticut 06902) 的 400 Washington Blvd.，電話號碼為 (203) 905-7801，並有可存取的網站 ir.charter.com。本公司年度報告書 (Form 10-K)、季報 (Form 10-Q) 及現況報告書 (Form 8-K) 以及所有相關修正案，均會在網站上免費提供，於相關文件提交後盡速提供。本網站所載資訊未經納入本年度報告書。

我們為客戶提供基於訂閱的網路、行動、視訊及語音服務，價格及相關費用根據所選服務類型、服務是否以「組合」方式銷售或個別銷售，以及接收我們服務所需的設備而定。組合服務，包括我們網路、行動、視訊及/或語音產品的一些組合，可供我們服務點的絕大多數客戶使用。

paragraphs: 請參閱「第一部分 第1A項 風險因素」及「關於前瞻性陳述的警示聲明」，這些內容說明瞭可能導致實際結果與預期及 herein 所含非歷史資訊有所差異的重要因素。此外，以下討論應與 Charter 所包含於「第二部分 第8項 財務報表及補充資料」中的審計合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。

我們是一家領先的寬頻連線公司，透過 Spectrum 品牌，服務範圍涵蓋美國41個州的5800萬戶家庭及中小企業。本公司於1993年成立，從提供有線電視演進至串流服務，從高速網路演進至整合型寬頻、WiFi及行動體驗。透過 Spectrum Fiber Broadband Network 並由我們100%美國籍員工支持，我們提供 Seamless Connectivity 和娛樂服務，包括 Spectrum Internet、Mobile、TV 和 Voice 產品。請參閱「第一部分 第1項 經營業務 — 產品與服務」以取得這些服務的進一步說明，包括不同服務的客戶統計資料。

截至2025年12月31日財年，我們新增了190萬條行動線路，而網際網路與視訊的流失情況相比前一財年有所改善。銷售受到競爭環境的挑戰，但因客戶流失率降低而有所抵銷。我們持續專注於透過品牌平台 Life Unlimited 改善客戶表現，該平台強調我們先進的光纖網路與尖端連線產品與服務的強大功能，以及我們簡化定價與包裝策略，更有效地利用我們的 Seamless Connectivity 和娛樂產品，提供更具競爭力的促銷與持續性捆綁定價，以推動成長。我們的網際網路與行動產品捆綁方案透過整合 Spectrum Internet、Advanced WiFi 與 Unlimited Spectrum Mobile，為消費者提供快速、可靠且安全的線上連線體驗，可在家中及行動設備上使用，並以高價值的捆綁方案提供。我們已與主要內容供應商達成協議，透過在部分 Spectrum TV 套餐中包含無額外費用的 Seamless 娛樂應用程式，為客戶提供更大的靈活性與價值。2025年7月，我們開始向客戶以點選式方式銷售這些 Seamless 娛樂應用程式，並最近推出了 Spectrum App Store，這是一個數位商店，協助客戶在一個地方啟動、升級、購買與管理其串流應用程式。我們也持續改進其他視訊產品的元素，並向新視訊客戶部署 Xumo 串流盒子。
我們的客戶承諾聚焦於可靠連線、透明度、卓越服務與持續改善。透過不斷改善產品組合，並為消費者提供轉換至我們服務以節省費用的機會，我們相信可以持續擴張我們的服務範圍，並向現有客戶銷售更多產品。我們從針對性投資員工薪資與福利以培養員工技能與服務年限，以及持續投資於客戶服務平台的數位化，看到了運營效益，所有這些投資的目標都是改善客戶體驗、減少交易次數，並推動客戶成長與留存。
我們在截至2025年12月31日財年，於 subsidiarized 鄉村建設計畫上支出22億美元，並啟動了約483,000個 subsidiarized 鄉村服務。我們目前提供 Spectrum Internet 產品，其速度可達1 Gbps，涵蓋我們整個服務範圍，並在部分服務範圍內提供多吉比特數據速度。我們的網路演進計畫持續進行中，目標是在我們所有運作地區提供對稱且多吉比特速度的連線。
我們在報告期間實現的收入、調整後營業利益及營業收入如下（以千萬為單位；所有百分比均以整數計算；因四捨五入可能有微小差異）。
調整後營業利益定義為歸屬於 Charter 股東的淨收入，加上歸屬於非控制性股東的淨收入，減去淨利息費用，減去所得稅，減去折舊與攤銷，減去股票薪酬費用，減去其他收入（費用），淨額，以及其他營運（收入）費用，淨額，例如特殊費用、合併與收購成本，以及資產出售或退休的損益。請參閱「—調整後營業利益與自由現金流」以取得調整後營業利益與自由現金流的進一步資訊。
總營業收入略微下降，主要由於客戶數量減少、無縫娛樂分配增加以及廣告銷售減少，部分抵銷了行動線路成長與每客戶平均收入增加。調整後的EBITDA略微成長，行動收入成長速度高於行動直接成本成長速度。營運收入進一步受到資產處置損失增加及合併與收購成本增加的負面影響。

我們於2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日結帳年度的營收約89%來自於客戶為我們的網路、行動、視訊、語音及商業服務以及區域體育與新聞頻道所支付的月費。通常，這些客戶訂閱可能在任何時間由客戶終止，但特定商業客戶需支付費用。剩餘11%的營收主要來自廣告收入、特許經營與其他規費收入（由我們收取後轉付地方機關）、行動與視訊裝置銷售、客戶啟用或恢復服務所收取的處理費或重新連線費、安裝費用、VOD與付費點播節目，以及居家購物服務銷售商品的佣金。
我們某些會計政策需要管理階層做出困難、主觀及/或複雜的判斷。管理階層已與Charter董事會的審計委員會討論這些政策，且審計委員會已審閱以下揭露。我們認為以下政策是理解財務報表所涉及的估計、假設與判斷，以及可能影響我們營運成果、財務狀況與現金流的不確定性最重要的政策：
•勞動與間接費用資本化 •特許經營與商譽的評價與減損

與網路建設或升級、客戶線路連接到住宅、住宅內裝置位置以及提供網路、視訊或語音服務所需新客戶端設備部署相關的費用，會被資本化。資本化的費用包括材料、直接勞動及某些間接費用。這些間接費用包含與支援功能相關的薪資與間接費用。雖然我們的資本化是根據特定活動進行，一旦資本化，我們會以有線電視系統層級的固定資產類別為基礎，以複合方式追蹤這些費用，而非以特定資產為基礎。對於已出售或停用的資產，我們會移除預估的相關費用及累計折舊。與中斷服務及移除客戶端設備相關的費用，以及重新連接客戶線路或重新部署已安裝的客戶端設備相關的費用，會在發生時計入營運費用。修繕與維護費用會在發生時計入營運費用，而設備更換，包括某些零組件更換、改善及電纜線路與裝置更換的費用，則會被資本化。
我們會對安裝與建設活動做出判斷以決定是否資本化。我們於2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日結帳年度分別資本化了26億美元與24億美元的直接勞動與間接費用。我們使用根據實際費用與適用運營數據所制定的標準來資本化直接勞動與間接費用。我們計算這些標準

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們營運於一個極其競爭的商業環境，這會影響我們吸引及留住客戶的能力，並可能對我們的業務、營運及財務結果產生不利影響。
各種事件可能幹擾或導致未經授權存取我們的網路、資訊系統或財產，並可能影響我們的營運活動，並對我們的聲譽及財務結果造成負面影響。
若無法回應科技發展及滿足客戶對新產品與服務的需求，可能對我們有效競爭的能力產生不利影響。
若我們無法持續取得或執行我們業務所依賴的智慧財產權權利，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們可能無法將程式製作成本的增加全部轉嫁給客戶，這可能會對我們的現金流及營運毛利產生不利影響。
與人工智慧（AI）的開發及使用相關的問題，可能引發法律或監管行動，損害我們的聲譽，或以其他方式對我們的業務造成重大損害。
我們對現有及潛在客戶、供應商及第三方的經濟狀況的敞口，可能對我們的現金流、營運結果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
若我們無法留住關鍵員工，將可能影響我們管理業務的能力。
與我們負債相關的風險
我們負債的契約及文據包含限制與限制，可能顯著影響我們經營業務的能力，同時也可能顯著影響我們的流動性。
與Liberty Broadband Corporation及Advance/Newhouse Partnership股權結構相關的風險
Liberty Broadband及A/N擁有治理權，使其能影響公司交易及其他事項。
與法規及立法事項相關的風險
我們的業務受到廣泛政府立法與監管，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們所處的法律與法規框架或我們或競爭對手參與的法規計畫發生變更，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
稅務法規及行政措施或對我們稅務及費用立場的挑戰，可能會不利於我們的營運成果與財務狀況。
Cox交易受條件限制，部分或全部條件可能無法達成，或無法及時完成，甚至可能無法完成。若無法完成Cox交易，可能會對我們造成重大不利影響。
Charter與Cox Communications在Cox交易進行期間，受合約限制，這可能會對其各自的業務與營運造成不利影響。
我們將因Cox交易而產生直接與間接的成本。
paragraphs: 我們所從事的產業具有高度競爭性，且近年來競爭程度更為激烈。在某些情況下，我們與具較少監管負擔、較佳融資管道及更強且更有利的品牌知名度的公司競爭。電信與內容產業的持續併購，已為部分競爭對手帶來額外優勢，包括透過融資管道、資源或規模經濟效益，例如發佈新產品與服務的能力。

我們的網路服務面臨來自其他公司 FTTH、行動電話提供的家庭網路服務、透過衛星與 DSL 服務提供網路的競爭。各種運營商提供透過網路提供的無線網路服務，並持續改善網路以提供更快的速度，同時也持續擴展 5G 移動服務，以提供與我們類似的整合式連線服務。我們的行動與語音服務與無線與有線電話服務供應商競爭，同時也與其他形式的通訊服務，例如簡訊、即時通訊、社交網路服務、視訊會議與電子郵件競爭。這些公司的競爭，包括強烈的行銷活動與激進的價格策略，可能對我們吸引與保留客戶的能力產生負面影響。
我們的視訊服務面臨來自多個來源的競爭，包括 DBS 服務，以及透過寬頻網路連線，向電視機、電腦、平板與行動裝置提供線性網路節目、電影與電視節目點播及其他視訊內容的公司，這些服務通常允許多用戶共用密碼，且安全性措施使內容容易遭盜版。較新的產品與服務，特別是內容分發、銷售與觀看的替代方法，可能持續被開發，進一步增加我們所面臨的競爭。
觀眾可選擇的項目越來越多，包括低成本或免費的選擇，可能不僅會對我們產品與服務的消費者需求產生負面影響，也會影響廣告客戶購買我們廣告的意願。我們與電影片道與電臺競爭廣告收入，同時也與其他廣告平台，例如線上媒體、廣播與印刷媒體競爭。我們對企業提供的服務競爭也持續增加，因為越來越多公司將光纖佈設至更多大樓，這可能對我們的成長產生負面影響，並對邊際毛利造成壓力。

未能有效預測或適應新技術（包括使用人工智慧（"AI"）的技術）與客戶期望與行為的變化，可能對我們在客戶閒暇時間與自由支配支出方面的競爭地位產生重大負面影響，進而影響我們的業務與營運成果。競爭也可能降低我們預期的未來現金流成長，這可能導致未來對我們特許經營權與商譽的減值，以及影響我們滿足現金流需求的能力，包括債務償還需求。有關我們所面臨的競爭，請參閱 "Item 1. Business - Competition" 以及 "Item 1. Business - Regulation and Legislation."

網路與資訊系統技術對我們的營運活動至關重要，不僅用於我們的內部用途，例如網路管理，也用於向客戶提供服務，包括客戶服務作業與節目傳輸。因電腦入侵、網路釣魚、散佈電腦病毒、蠕蟲及其他破壞或幹擾軟體、國家威脅行為者所進行的惡意網路活動、"網路攻擊"（例如勒索軟體）、程序中斷、拒絕服務攻擊及其他惡意活動所導致的網路或資訊系統中斷或服務中斷，會帶來日益增加的風險。近年來，未成功與成功的 "網路攻擊" 在頻率、範圍與潛在損害方面持續增加，而人工智能的日益應用可能使這些網路安全風險更加嚴重。雖然我們開發並維護系統以防止系統相關事件與安全事件的發生，但這些系統的開發與維護成本高昂，且需要持續監測與更新，以應對這些攻擊技術變得更加複雜且頻繁變化的趨勢。我們與我們所依賴的第三方，可能無法預測這些技術或實施適當的預防措施。雖然有時會有嘗試入侵我們網路的行為，但這些事件迄今尚未導致任何重大資訊外洩、網路與資訊系統的效能退化或中斷。
